svg.title: Four steps from the opening prompt to a card in your wallet
svg.desc: Four steps side by side, joined by arrows. Step one is the opening prompt: replace the origin, destination and length of stay with your own details and paste it to the AI to set the role. You only fill this in once. Step two is five sets of questions, copied and pasted item by item with no editing: the digital environment covering censorship, Tor, VPN and device searches; legal and political risk; connectivity and communication covering SIM and eSIM; emergency contacts and support networks; and, optionally, the physical and surveillance environment. Step three is checking against primary sources, taking the AI's answers to the official sources listed at the foot of the article, with emergency numbers, statute references, visa rules and tariffs always verified. Step four is the emergency card: copy the key contacts from the fourth set of questions onto a card, print and laminate it, keep one in your wallet and one in your luggage, and store a copy in an offline note on your phone. The red box at the bottom warns that AI invents phone numbers, statutes and tariffs.
svg.text: length of stay with your own details.
Dates and identity can be left blank.
Paste it to the AI to set the role.
The full version for self-hosted and local
models. The commercial version drops details
that would be retained in the conversation.
Copy and paste, no editing needed
Take the AI's answers to the official
sources listed at the foot of the article.
Copy the key contacts from the fourth set of
questions onto a card. Print and laminate it,
one in your wallet and one in your
luggage. Store a copy in an offline note.
Language models are very good at
answers as a list of what to look up
next rather than as the final answer.
The more obscure the destination and the thinner
the public record, the less training data the
model has and the more it invents, which is
exactly where reliable information matters most.
